$comment: Measured upstream-endpoint preferences for the dictation clean-up call.
WHAT THIS FILE IS. One OpenRouter model id is served by many upstream
endpoints and OpenRouter picks one per request, so without a preference every
dictation is a lottery over the whole spread below. This file records a
measurement and names the order to prefer. It is DATA, not code, for one
reason: it goes stale. The pool moves under a model id (on this same id
AtlasCloud now answers HTTP 400 and DeepInfra 404), so the order is a
preference that is never a requirement, and unknown names are skipped.
THIS FILE IS OPTIONAL. Delete it, point DICTATION_REFINE_ENDPOINTS at a
missing path, or ship a build without it: refine still works. The loader
falls back to an empty order, which means OpenRouter's own price/uptime
balancing. What does NOT depend on this file is the reasoning-violator
denylist -- that lives in providers.py, because it is a correctness and cost
guard rather than a latency preference, and losing it to a missing data file
would quietly quadruple the bill.
HOW THE ORDER WAS CHOSEN. Latency medians support 'CoreWeave-class vs Novita'
(a ~16x spread) and 'these three ignore the off switch'. They do NOT support
fine ordering within the fast group -- those ranges overlap too heavily for a
user to tell apart. So within the fast group the tie is broken on cost, which
is measured off token counts rather than a median: CoreWeave first (fastest
and second-cheapest, nothing to trade), then GMICloud (cheapest, speed
indistinguishable from ModelRun), then ModelRun.
HOW TO RE-MEASURE. Same build, same Product Profile, medians over repeats on
one machine; record wall seconds, TTFT, tok/s, completion tokens, and whether
reasoning:{enabled:false} was honoured. Replace 'measured' below and bump
measured_on. Do not edit 'order' without replacing the table that justifies it.
SambaNova and Mara are deliberately absent from 'order': slowest of the
group that honours the off switch AND dearest (~5x GMICloud). Absent from
'order' does not mean excluded -- allow_fallbacks can still land there if
everything above is down, which is the right trade against no text at all.
measurement_limits: One machine, one network, one time of day. Supports the ~16x spread and the off-switch finding; not the fine ordering inside the fast group.
The two fastest are fp4. Clean-up QUALITY per quantisation is UNMEASURED, so this order buys latency with an unmeasured precision trade.
usd_per_1000_dictations is list price applied to tokens really spent, for a ~138-visible-word dictation. It is why the three off-switch violators cost 3-5x on the same list price.
Measured on minimax/minimax-m3 only. For any other model id these names are a preference its pool may not contain.
naming_caveat: OpenRouter documents order/ignore/only as taking provider SLUGS, but these are the provider_name DISPLAY strings reported by /endpoints -- which are what the study confirmed working in 'order'. A slug is not the lowercased name (AtlasCloud -> atlas-cloud/fp8, not atlascloud).
If that ever diverges, the client drops the provider block and retries once at default routing rather than failing the dictation.
